blocks.h2: Common Reasons to Get a Sewer Camera Inspection
blocks.intro: Homeowners aren't always having sewer problems when they book a camera inspection. Here's when it's worth a look:

tiles.h3: Drains That Clog or Back Up More Than Once
tiles.body: Recurring backups, sewage odors, or unexplained water damage and mold are all signs it's worth having your line inspected. The camera shows what's going on instead of guessing.

tiles.h3: Buying an Older North Shore Home
tiles.body: About 1 in 4 Highland Park homes was built before 1940. We'll show you the condition of the sewer line before you buy or sell, so there are no surprises after closing.
If you're planning to remodel a kitchen or bathroom, a camera inspection helps you understand if your plumbing can handle the new fixtures before work starts.
Dropping a ring down the drain doesn't mean it's lost forever. Our camera can help you locate jewelry and other valuables inside the line.

blocks.h2: What We Look for in Highland Park Sewer Lines
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, many on wooded lots near ravines. That shapes what the camera tends to find.

items.body: Clay is common in homes built before the 1980s and prone to root intrusion and cracked joints. Tree roots work through small cracks or loose joints and grow inside the line, restricting flow.
Cast iron was built to last decades but corrodes and cracks from the inside as it ages. The camera shows scale, pitting and cracks you'd never see from the basement.
A belly is a low spot where water and waste collect instead of draining, usually from ground settling. Years of freeze-thaw can also pull two pipe sections apart at the joint.

In Highland Park, the homeowner owns the private sewer line from the house to the city main. The city's own flood tips recommend having it checked for roots and debris. The camera is how you know what's in it.

blocks.h2: How a Sewer Camera Inspection Works
blocks.intro: No digging required. Here's exactly how we get eyes on your sewer line and what you walk away with.

steps.body: We locate your main drain cleanout, whether it's inside or outside your home. That's where the camera goes in: no digging, no cutting into walls or floors.
We send in a waterproof camera with strong LED lighting, built to travel through the pipe and send back a clear, real-time picture of what's inside.

We watch the footage live with you and mark the exact location of anything we find: root intrusion, cracks, corrosion, blockages, pipe separation, or offset joints. We save the footage and give you a copy for your records.

blocks.h2: Camera Inspection Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Should I get a sewer camera inspection before buying a home in Highland Park?
items.preview: Yes. Many homes here are older, and the buyer takes over the private sewer line.
items.answer: It's a smart step, especially here. About 45% of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, often with clay or cast iron sewer lines, and the buyer takes over the private line from the house to the city main. A camera inspection shows the real condition before you close.

items.q: How often should I have my sewer line inspected?
items.preview: Every few years for older homes with trees nearby, or any time drains slow down or gurgle.
items.answer: There's no fixed schedule, but older homes with mature trees nearby benefit from a camera inspection every few years, or any time you notice slow drains or gurgling. An inspection shows the condition of your line so you can fix small problems early. See [sewer maintenance](/highland-park/sewer-maintenance) for a regular schedule.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost?
items.preview: Cost depends on the length of your line, access points, and what we find along the way.
items.answer: The cost depends on factors like the length of your line, how many access points we need to check, and what we find along the way. Give us a call and we'll walk you through it.

items.q: Will a sewer camera inspection damage my pipes or my property?
items.preview: No. We access your line through an existing cleanout, so no digging or cutting is required.
items.answer: No. We access your line through an existing cleanout, so there's no digging or cutting into walls or floors. If a cleanout is hard to reach, we'll tell you rather than force our way in.

items.q: What happens if the camera finds a problem?
items.preview: We show you the footage, explain your options and give you a flat price. You decide what's next.
items.answer: We show you the footage, mark the exact location and explain your options in plain language. That could be [sewer rodding](/highland-park/sewer-rodding), [hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) or a [sewer repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair). You get a flat price before any work, and nothing happens until you decide.
